point_estimate_why: Two reasons that do not go away. (1) The boundary between a claim default and a definitional value is a domain fact absent from the AST; four calls in one function split two-and-two, so any single number implies a classification the instrument cannot perform. (2) The scope question was never ruled and the two halves of the existing headline answered it differently, so a point estimate would silently pick one. The prior pass corrected 0.4%; the real correction is 23% to 45%, in both directions at once.

three_question_gate.executes: Nothing on a trigger. A human runs `python apps/cockpit/backend/scripts/audit_default_shapes.py` from the repo root. Its TEST runs in CI under `python -m pytest -q`, but that pins the instrument's own behaviour, not the codebase's defaulting constructs.
three_question_gate.triggers: For the script, a human deciding to look. For the test, every CI run on every push and PR.
three_question_gate.fails: Nothing fails on a new defaulting construct; the script exits 0 by design and reports a candidate count. The test fails, in CI today, only if someone changes the predicate, the exclusions, or the false-negative sizing without updating the fixture. That is drift protection for the instrument, not enforcement against the code.
three_question_gate.bypasses: Any defaulting construct in the 296 unconfigured files; any of the nine sized false-negative shapes; any construct added to a configured file, since no baseline is stored and nothing recomputes or compares a count over time. There is nothing to diverge from.
three_question_gate.honest_label: DIAGNOSTIC. Making it a control needs a committed per-file baseline and a CI job failing on increase. That was not built, and claiming otherwise would be the defect this programme keeps finding.
